title: How long does the tap take to fill the bucket?
description: A tap fills a five hundred millilitre mug in fifteen seconds. The video changes the ten litre bucket to millilitres, finds the factor of change in volume, and scales the time by it.
teaching_notes: One idea: put both volumes in the same unit, then the time changes by the same factor as the volume. Watch for students who compare ten with five hundred and forget that litres and millilitres differ.

video_script.why: A tap gives water at a steady rate, so time and volume are in proportion once both volumes are in the same unit.
video_script.substitution: Change litres to millilitres, divide the new volume by the old volume to get the factor, and multiply the time by it.
video_script.anchor: a tap filling a mug and then a bucket, from the book
video_script.payoff_line: The tap takes three hundred seconds, which is five minutes

final_answer.spoken: three hundred seconds, which is five minutes

never_show: 10 ÷ 500 as the factor of change, marked as right
video_script.design: One idea: same unit first, then one factor of change for both volume and time. The tap, the mug and the bucket stay on the stage and the working shows the factor.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a tap.
<bookmark mark='mug'/>The tap takes fifteen seconds to fill a mug of water. The mug holds five hundred millilitres.
<bookmark mark='bucket'/>The same tap now fills a bucket that holds ten litres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much time will the same tap take to fill the whole bucket of water?

beats.on_screen: the tap holds still and the question mark clock glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

beats.on_screen: the tap delivers equal streams; the volume bar and the time bar grow together; 1 litre = 1000 mL appears beside a measuring jug

marks.same: the tap delivers equal streams and the volume bar and time bar grow together
marks.unit: the two volume labels are linked and must match
marks.litre: 1 litre = 1000 mL appears beside a measuring jug

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>The same tap gives the same amount of water every second. The time and the volume stay in proportion.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Both volumes must be written in the same unit before we compare them.
<bookmark mark='litre'/>One litre of water is the same as one thousand millilitres of water.

beats.on_screen: Given: 500 mL takes 15 seconds; the bucket holds 10 litres

marks.given: the mug volume, its time and the bucket volume are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the tap takes fifteen seconds to fill five hundred millilitres, and the bucket holds ten litres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the time to fill the bucket

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the time the tap takes to fill the bucket.
<bookmark mark='conv'/>Step one, change the bucket to millilitres. Ten litres is ten times one thousand, which is ten thousand millilitres.

marks.factor: 10000 ÷ 500 = 20 is written on an arrow from the mug to the bucket

narration: <bookmark mark='factor'/>Step two, find the factor of change in volume. Ten thousand divided by five hundred is twenty.
<bookmark mark='time'/>Step three, the time changes by the same factor. Twenty times fifteen is three hundred.
<bookmark mark='min'/>Step four, change the seconds to minutes. Three hundred divided by sixty is five.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check. Twenty mugs of five hundred millilitres make ten thousand millilitres.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed beside the bucket

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The tap takes three hundred seconds, which is five minutes.
